buyer_question: We currently use stdlib json. simplejson advertises itself as 'fast' with a C extension for 'a serious speed boost' — is that actually faster than the stdlib json shipped with our Python today, and are the compatibility claims (3.9+, 3.14 free-threaded, Python 2.7 wheel) real?

claims.text: The package simplejson installs from PyPI with `pip install simplejson` and `import simplejson` then works on Python 3.9+.
claims.source_quote:
simplejson is a simple, fast, complete, correct and extensible
JSON <http://json.org> encoder and decoder for Python 3.9+
claims.probe_hint: Fresh venv on current Python: `pip install simplejson`, then `python -c "import simplejson; print(simplejson.dumps({'a':1}))"` expecting {"a": 1}.

claims.text: simplejson is fast, and includes an optional C extension providing 'a serious speed boost' — implying encode/decode meaningfully faster than pure-Python operation and competitive with or better than stdlib json.
claims.source_quote:
It is pure Python code
with no dependencies, but includes an optional C extension
for a serious speed boost.
claims.probe_hint: Benchmark on one machine, same interpreter: timeit dumps/loads of (a) a large nested dict/list document and (b) many small documents, comparing simplejson-with-C-extension vs simplejson pure-Python (simplejson._toggle_speedups(False) or py impl) vs stdlib json. Report x-factors. The C-vs-pure-simplejson boost is the literal claim; the buyer-relevant comparison is vs stdlib json (which has its own C accelerator and often wins).

claims.text: simplejson is pure Python code with no dependencies.
claims.source_quote:
It is pure Python code
with no dependencies, but includes an optional C extension
for a serious speed boost.
claims.probe_hint: pip install in a clean venv and confirm no other distributions are installed. Note the internal tension: the same sentence claims 'pure Python' AND a bundled C extension — wheels ship compiled _speedups; 'pure Python' is only true of the fallback path. Verify import succeeds with the C extension disabled/absent.

claims.text: This version is tested with Python 3.14, including free-threaded builds, and maintains backwards compatibility with Python 3.9+.
claims.source_quote:
This version is tested
with Python 3.14 (including free-threaded builds) and maintains
backwards compatibility with Python 3.9+.
claims.probe_hint: Inspect .github/workflows at the pinned SHA for a 3.14 (and 3.14t free-threaded) matrix entry and check the latest run status; optionally run the test suite on a 3.14 interpreter.

claims.text: A legacy Python 2.7 wheel of simplejson is also published (legacy support for Python 2.7).
claims.source_quote: with legacy support for Python 2.7.  It is pure Python code
claims.probe_hint: Query PyPI JSON API for the latest simplejson release and check for a cp27/py2 wheel filename among the published files.

claims.text: The RawJSON example works exactly as printed: dumps({"status": "ok", "data": RawJSON('{"a": 1, "b": 2}')}) outputs {"status": "ok", "data": {"a": 1, "b": 2}}.
claims.probe_hint: Run the exact snippet from the README (`from simplejson import dumps, RawJSON`) and compare stdout literally, including key order and spacing.

claims.text: RawJSON embedding works in both the C-extension and pure-Python encoder paths.
claims.source_quote:
``RawJSON`` allows embedding pre-encoded JSON strings into output without
re-encoding them.
claims.probe_hint: Run the c6 snippet twice: once normally (C speedups active) and once with speedups disabled (simplejson._toggle_speedups(False) or SIMPLEJSON_PURE env), asserting identical output.

claims.text: The encoder can serialize arbitrary objects without their cooperation via the `default` kwarg to dumps.
claims.source_quote:
The encoder can be specialized to provide serialization in any kind of
situation, without any special support by the objects to be serialized
(somewhat like pickle). This is best done with the ``default`` kwarg
to dumps.
claims.probe_hint: dumps(CustomClass(), default=lambda o: {'x': o.x}) should succeed and emit the transformed dict.

claims.text: The decoder can post-process JSON objects via the `object_hook` or `object_pairs_hook` kwargs.
claims.source_quote:
It can also be specialized to post-process JSON
objects with the ``object_hook`` or ``object_pairs_hook`` kwargs.
claims.probe_hint: loads('{"a": 1}', object_pairs_hook=collections.OrderedDict) returns an OrderedDict; object_hook receives each decoded dict.

claims.text: Documentation is available online at https://simplejson.readthedocs.io/.
claims.source_quote:
The latest documentation for simplejson can be read online here:
https://simplejson.readthedocs.io/
claims.probe_hint: HTTP GET the URL, expect 200 and a docs page for the current version.

claims.text: A very old Python 2.2-compatible fork exists on the `python2.2` branch of the repository (unmaintained, last resort).
claims.source_quote:
there is a
very old fork of simplejson in the `python2.2`_ branch that supports
Python 2.2.
